question: Which of the following is the unit of electrical resistance?
solution:
The correct answer is __Ohm__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Electrical Resistance

 
 
• A measurement of an object's resistance to the flow of electrical current is called its electrical resistance.
 
• An object's resistance is mostly determined by the substance from which it is formed; for example, rubber-manufactured items typically have very high resistance and low conductivity.
 
• The ratio of the voltage (V) applied across an object to the current (I) flowing through it is known as its resistance (R). 
 
• Ohm (Ω) is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
 
• A conductor's electrical resistance depends on the following factors:
 
 
• Size of the conductor
 
• The cross-sectional area of the wire
 
• Composition of the conductor and
 
• Temperature
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 SI unit
 Quantity
 
 

 Watt (W)
 
 
 
• Unit of power
 
• 1 W = 1.00 joules per second (J/sec)
 
• It is named after James Watt
 
• Power is defined as the amount of energy transferred per unit of time.
 
 
 
 

 Coulomb (C)
 
 
 
• Unit of electrical charge
 
• Named after Charles-Augustin de Coulomb, a French scientist.
 
• One coulomb is equal to one ampere (A) of current flowing for one second (s).
 
 
 
 

 Newton (N)
 
 
 
• Unit of force
 
• Named after Issac Newton
 
• One Newton is the force that, when applied to a body of mass 1 kg, will give an acceleration of 1ms-2
